name: Rotational Power
pages: {b}Rotational power{/} refers to the mechanical force used by Create mod components, such as spinning shafts and turning gears. There are two aspects to rotational power: speed and stress.{pb}{b}Speed{/} is measured in {t:revolutions per minute}RPM{/t}. Components using rotational power can have a speed up to 256 RPM, but will break if they exceed that limit.

{b}Stress{/} is measured in {t:stress units}SU{/t}. This tells you how much power a component is {i}consuming{/} or {i}generating{/}. The stress consumed or generated by a component depends on its current speed.{pb}For example, the {b}millstone{/} has a stress value of 4, meaning it will consume 4 times its speed in SU. So a millstone spinning at 10 RPM will consume 40 SU, but reducing its speed to 5 RPM will also reduce its consumption to 20 SU.

All rotational components that are connected together by cogwheels, shafts, or other rotational components belong to a {b}network{/}. Any components that {i}generate{/} SU add that to the network's total capacity. Any components that {i}consume{/} SU subtract that from the network's total capacity.{pb}If a network has more SU being consumed than generated, it will become {b}overstressed{/}, making all its components stop.

There are two ways to fix an overstressed network: either {b}reduce the amount of stress{/} being consumed by slowing down some or removed of its components, or {b}increase the total capacity{/} by adding or speeding up components that generate stress.{pb}Once a network is no longer overstressed, it will start rotating again. You can use a {b}stressometer{/} or {b}speedometer{/} to read a network's stress or speed with {b}goggles{/} equipped.
